cards.front: Recall a key point about NEA Coursework Guide
cards.back: NEA = Non-Exam Assessment, worth 50% of GCSE D&T. Students complete a single design-and-make task from a choice of contextual challenges set by AQA. Approximately 35 hours of supervised time.

cards.front: Recall a key point about NEA Coursework Guide
cards.back: NEA structure: Section 1 - Investigating (research, design brief, specification), Section 2 - Designing (ideas, development, modelling), Section 3 - Making (manufacturing the prototype), Section 4 - Analysing and Evaluating (testing against specification, improvements).

cards.front: Recall a key point about NEA Coursework Guide
cards.back: Portfolio: A3 format (or digital equivalent), 20-30 pages recommended. Each section must be clearly labelled. Include photographs of making, annotated sketches, test results, evaluation against specification points.

cards.front: Recall a key point about NEA Coursework Guide
cards.back: Marking criteria: AO1 - Investigating (10%), AO2 - Designing (20%), AO3 - Making (30%), AO4 - Analysing and Evaluating (15%). Each AO has specific mark bands - read the criteria and target the top band.

cards.front: Recall a key point about NEA Coursework Guide
cards.back: Time management: 35 hours total - Investigating approx 8 hrs, Designing approx 10 hrs, Making approx 12 hrs, Evaluating approx 5 hrs. Common mistake: spending too long on research and not enough on making and evaluation.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For NEA questions: 1) Identify which section the question relates to, 2) Describe what that section requires, 3) Explain how to present evidence effectively, 4) Link to the marking criteria (AO1-AO4), 5) Give specific practical advice for maximising marks.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: The NEA prototype needs to be a perfect, professional-quality product that looks like something from a shop. Correct: The NEA prototype is a proof-of-concept that demonstrates your design works - it does NOT need to look like a manufactured product. AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). The NEA specifically assesses AO1 Investigating (10%), AO2 Designing (20%), AO3 Making (30%), AO4 Analysing & Evaluating (15%).

The AQA GCSE D&T NEA (Non-Exam Assessment) is worth 50% of the final grade and consists of a single design-and-make task completed in approximately 35 hours of supervised time. The NEA is structured into four sections: Investigating (16 marks), Designing (32 marks), Making (32 marks), and Analysing and Evaluating (12 marks), totalling 92 raw marks. The NEA portfolio is typically presented as an A3 document (approximately 20 pages) or a digital equivalent. Each page should have a clear heading, organised content and concise annotation. Photographs must be high-quality, well-lit and clearly show the relevant detail. Sketches should be annotated with specific design decisions rather than generic labels.
